The advanced age is not necessarily a contraindication to GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease) laparoscopic surgery. In fact, several studies suggest that patients with advanced age can safely undergo this procedure and may even experience improved outcomes compared to younger patients.

According to the available information, Laparoscopic antireflux surgery is a safe and effective treatment for GERD, warranting low morbidity and mortality rates and a significant improvement in symptoms comparable to younger patients. Patients over 70 years old are generally considered to be candidates for this procedure, although the decision should be made on a case-by-case basis.

The American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ASGE) recommends that laparoscopic antireflux surgery be performed in patients with GERD symptoms, including those with advanced age, provided that they have failed medical therapy and are at high risk of complications. The goal is to alleviate symptoms and improve quality of life.

However, it's essential to note that the decision to undergo surgery should take into account various factors, such as overall health, comorbidities, and a thorough assessment by a qualified healthcare professional. Patients over 70 years old may require more caution and careful evaluation before undergoing laparoscopic antireflux surgery.

In summary, while advanced age is not necessarily a contraindication to GERD laparoscopic surgery, it's crucial for patients over this age group to be carefully evaluated and considered on a case-by-case basis.
